records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:13 — [P1, confidence 100] `return Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1;` reports a second page for every group whose membership count is exactly a multiple of the page limit, so admins navigate to an empty members page instead of seeing the complete membership list.
records.rationale: The diff shows totalPages = Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. With user_count exactly a multiple of limit (e.g. 100 members, limit 50), totalPages = 3, but only 2 pages of members exist; currentPage can equal totalPages (showingLast not yet true), letting admins navigate to an empty page. The off-by-one mechanism is verifiable directly from the diffed formula.

records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:45 — [P1, confidence 100] `self.findMembers();` reloads the now-invalid last-page offset after deleting the only member on that page, so a 51-member group reduced to 50 displays an empty second page and leaves the remaining 50 members inaccessible through the current pagination controls.
records.rationale: The mechanism is verifiable in the diff: `removeMember` calls `self.findMembers()` with the unchanged `offset`, and `findMembers` clamps offset using the stale pre-reload `user_count` (`Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0))`), so deleting the only member of the last page can request an offset past the new total, yielding an empty list. This paging logic is newly introduced by this diff, so the defect is introduced here.

records.rationale: The diff shows `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` with no upper bound in the public groups_controller#members action, and the members query uses that limit directly.
